Stage 2 always uses the actual price-responsive EV load simulated for the specified mechanism (RTP or TOU), flexibility type (within-session or within-week), and participation level. No-foresight uses the Stage 1 simulation with unmanaged EV load to establish initial commitment and scheduling decisions for Stage 2. This is a worst-case forecast, in which the day-ahead unit commitment does not anticipate how EVs will respond to RTP or TOU prices. Perfect-foresight uses the same EV load profiles as Stage 2 in Stage 1. Thus, Stage 2 is initialized with commitment decisions and dispatch levels that already anticipate the exact shape of EV load—a best-case forecast. 2.6 Scenario Framework This study compares the production cost (PC) savings of EVMC across participation mechanisms (DLC-LE, RTP, TOU), participation rates (5%, 30%, 60%, 100%), forecasting types (no-foresight and perfect-foresight), and flexibility types (within-session, within-week) (Table 2). Relative to our previous work (Hale et al. 2022a), which used only no-foresight forecasts for the price- responsive RTP and TOU mechanisms, this study measures the extent to which perfect-foresight forecasts improve RTP and TOU performance relative to no-foresight forecasts and to DLC-LE, which we assume to be perfectly forecast because it directly coordinates EV charging with supply-side grid resources (with low error). We calculate EVMC production cost savings by subtracting the production costs of the managed scenarios from those of the reference, unmanaged, scenario. We report results in dollars per participating vehicle-year ($/veh-yr), in absolute dollars, and as a percentage of the unmanaged scenario’s production costs.
